narrative: Material PL3__M05EDAA4 exhibits erratic demand with a 75% activity rate and a CV of ~59%, driven by frequent zero-demand gaps and periodic demand spikes. Lead times are highly unstable (CV ~81%), ranging from 0.5 to 3.7 days, making buffer stock essential. A (r,Q) continuous review policy with a 798-unit safety stock and 1,818-unit order quantity achieves the 95% service level target while cutting total annual costs by 68%. The order quantity is constrained by the 2,616-unit storage ceiling, preventing full realization of the EOQ; capacity expansion should be evaluated.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: EOQ 3807 reduced to 1818 units.
Lead time is highly unstable (CV=80.62%); safety stock formula based on combined variance.
2 demand outliers detected and winsorized at 99th percentile.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic but largely continuous demand with highly variable lead times favours a continuous-review reorder-point system. The (r,Q) model reacts immediately when inventory drops to the reorder point, minimising stock-out exposure during long lead-time realisations, and the fixed order quantity enables bulk purchase efficiency.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap (2,616 units) forces order quantity to 1,818, well below the unconstrained EOQ of 3,807. This increases ordering frequency and adds ~$3,462/year in avoidable ordering costs. If safety stock needs to be raised due to increased demand volatility, the available order window shrinks further, potentially pushing below MOQ.
research_insights.escalation_flag: No MOQ-capacity infeasibility detected (MOQ 411 + SS 798 = 1,209 < 2,616). Capacity expansion ROI analysis is recommended to unlock full EOQ savings.
